Discoverer: Adam Cazzolla of Sonatype Security Research
Method of Attack: ReDoS vulnerabilities commonly occur when the regex being used to evaluate a string doesn’t take into account the numerous paths a regex engine will have to take during their evaluation, leading to catastrophic backtracking. In such an event, the regex matching engine consumes a large amount of CPU and/or memory resources. If a skilled attacker crafts a malicious input, a DoS condition will occur on the target host, all because of a string matching operation taking up much of the available resources.
